questions.stem:
When the old post office in Aremo village was converted into a public library, many residents thought the project would fail within a few months. The building had a leaking roof, the shelves were uneven and the first collection of books looked too small to attract serious readers. Yet the youth corps members who supervised the renovation believed that the library could become more than a room filled with dusty pages. They organized evening reading circles, invited retired teachers to tell stories and set up a corner where farmers could read pamphlets on soil improvement and crop storage. At first, children came mainly for the free biscuits sometimes shared after the reading sessions. Before long, however, they began to compete over who would finish a novel first. Adults who had not entered a classroom in years started to use the library to fill forms, check agricultural notices and prepare for professional examinations. The library did not solve every problem in the village, but it quietly changed what many people thought education was for.

The passage is mainly about how the library

options.A: failed because the building was too old
options.B: became useful by changing how villagers viewed education
options.C: was built by retired teachers alone
options.D: was meant only for children who liked novels

questions.stem:
At the Federal College campus, students complain loudly whenever the taps run dry, yet few notice the rainwater that disappears from the roofs after every storm. Last year, the environmental club proposed that each hostel should channel roof water into storage tanks for cleaning, gardening and emergency use. Some students laughed at the idea and called it a poor substitute for government responsibility. The club members replied that conserving water was not an attempt to excuse official failure but a practical response to an urgent need. After a pilot scheme was installed in one hostel, the benefits became visible. The hostel used less treated water for washing corridors, the vegetable garden behind the cafeteria remained green during a brief shortage, and maintenance workers reported fewer quarrels at the public taps. The project did not end all scarcity, but it showed that careful planning can reduce waste. What had looked like a desperate improvisation gradually appeared to be an intelligent habit.

The writer's main purpose in the passage is to

options.A: mock students who live in hostels
options.B: show that a practical conservation idea can reduce water waste
options.C: argue that government should never provide water
options.D: prove that only environmental clubs understand science

questions.stem:
Sade joined Madam Bisi's tailoring shop because her family needed extra income, but she soon discovered that sewing demanded more discipline than she had imagined. Needles had to be arranged carefully, measurements recorded accurately and fabrics cut with patience rather than excitement. In her first week, she spoiled an expensive Ankara material by trimming the sleeve too short. Expecting a harsh rebuke, she stood silently beside the cutting table. Madam Bisi only asked her to explain what she had done and why she had rushed. Then she made Sade use a leftover piece of cloth to practise sleeve patterns until closing time. Months later, customers began to request Sade's finishing because her stitches were neat and her buttonholes sat evenly. She still worked slowly, but she no longer mistook speed for skill. The shop taught her more than a trade. It showed her that embarrassment can become instruction when pride does not prevent learning.

Which statement best expresses the controlling idea of the passage?

options.A: Tailoring requires discipline, and mistakes can become part of learning
options.B: Customers always prefer neat buttonholes to fast service
options.C: Family poverty is the only reason apprentices enter tailoring
options.D: Ankara material is the hardest fabric to cut

questions.stem:
During the dry season, the village stream often shrank and left residents struggling for clean water. The community association responded by repairing old boreholes, setting rules against wasteful use and creating a rotation schedule for water collection. Although the dry season remained severe, tension reduced and access became fairer.

What can be inferred from the passage?

options.A: Scarcity can be managed better when people cooperate and follow rules.
options.B: Rules are unnecessary in times of shortage.
options.C: The stream was the only possible water source.
options.D: The community solved all water problems permanently.
